name: Should I build out with a ground-level bump-out or add a second story?

mainEntity.name: Should I build out with a ground-level bump-out or add a second story?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ground-level bump-outs expand your ground-floor footprint, while second-story additions build upward over existing rooms. A ground-level addition preserves your home’s existing roof and upper structure but sacrifices yard space and requires adequate property setbacks. A second-story addition protects your yard area, which is helpful on narrow urban lots, but it requires reinforcing existing foundations, retrofitting lower-level load-bearing walls, and installing a new staircase, which removes some square footage from the main floor.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building out preserves your existing structure but uses yard space; building up protects your lot size but requires foundation reinforcement and interior staircase space.
